title: Detailing, restoration and the scope of a service
audience: Car detailers who write quotes and work orders, and who decide what is in and out of scope.
learningOutcomes: Explain the difference between detailing and restoration, using the source definitions.
Classify a booking as basic, full, commercial or show detailing, and describe what each includes.
Refer restoration, body repair and other specialist work to an appropriate provider instead of promising it as detailing.

instruction.heading: What detailing is
instruction.body: Detailing is a total cleaning of a vehicle, inside and out, top to bottom, with each surface treated to suit its material. The Detailing Hand Book describes it as more than a good wash and wax. The small things decide the result: wax buildup around trim, dirt in the seams, and grime in the wheel wells are the details that separate a detailed car from a washed one. The handbook stresses that choosing the correct chemical, wax or sealer for each surface is one of the most important things a detailer learns, because the correct treatment protects the surface as well as improving its appearance. Detailing works with the vehicle's existing finish. It cleans, corrects within agreed limits, and protects.

instruction.heading: Detailing versus restoration
instruction.body: Restoration returns a car to its original condition. The handbook describes it as tearing the car apart, examining each part, reworking or replacing it, and reassembling it with great care. That is time-consuming and costly, and most cars do not need it. Detailing does not dismantle the vehicle. The handbook makes a practical point: even a restored show car is detailed before a show, because detailing makes a car look its best. The source overview describes detailing as restoring a car to its original condition, which conflicts with the handbook. This lesson uses the handbook's distinction, because it matches the scope of the course. Replacing a part, re-spraying, or fixing a cracked lens or dashboard is outside detailing, and should be referred. This course also treats spray painting, live electrical work, airbag work and hazardous remediation as outside its scope.

instruction.heading: Service types
instruction.body: Booking types differ in scope. A basic detail covers exterior washing, waxing and interior cleaning, and suits regular maintenance. A full detail adds polishing, waxing and conditioning of the interior, and takes several hours. A mobile detail is the same kind of service delivered at the customer's home or office, which adds water, power and site questions (see “Manual handling, wet floors and site hygiene” and “Service boundaries and consent”). A commercial or used-car preparation is a minor detail that makes a car presentable for sale, done quickly. The handbook warns that quick services sometimes use a clear lacquer to make engine bays and trims look new, which can trap dirt under the cover. A fast finish is a different service with a different promise, and it must be described as such. A show detail is the most complete and the most time-consuming. The handbook notes that, except to the sharpest eye, there is little visual difference between complete and show detailing on an ordinary vehicle.

instruction.heading: Dents, chips and other repairs
instruction.body: The Detailing Hand Book lists minor dent removal and paint-chip touch-up among the services of a complete detailing shop. In this course the approach is different. A dent that needs reshaping, a chip that needs touch-up paint, or a scratch that needs filler is a repair with its own materials, skills and promises. Treat repair as a separate service with its own scope and quote, and do not describe it as part of the detail unless the business has the skill and the authority to carry it out. Where a repair is to be referred, say so in the work order and record the referral.

procedure: Ask the owner what the vehicle needs, and list each requested item.
Classify each item as detailing, commercial preparation, or a repair or restoration item.
Write the scope into the work order, with the exclusions stated.
Quote the detailing scope separately from any repair, or refer the repair and record the referral.
Confirm the finish and the time the booking allows, and do not promise more.
Give the owner the work order and keep a copy in the job file.

workedExamples.situation: An owner books a full detail and asks for a dent to be removed and a cracked dashboard fixed at the same time.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you write the work order?
workedExamples.reasoning: Write the full detail as the detailing scope. List the dent and the cracked dashboard as separate items that are not included, and refer them to a repairer. Give the owner a clear record of what the price covers. Do not add the repairs to the detailing price without a separate scope and quote.

workedExamples.situation: A dealer asks for a show finish on a used car that is being listed for sale within two hours.
workedExamples.reasoning: A show finish is the most complete and most time-consuming service, and cannot be delivered in two hours. Offer a commercial preparation scope that cleans, treats and presents the car within the time, and state its limits in writing. Do not use a lacquer or cover-up product that hides defects.

equipmentAndPpe: Work order template with service tiers, exclusions and a referral line.
Condition record from “Vehicle condition and evidence”.
PPE: none specific to this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Calling a restoration or repair 'detailing' in a quote.
commonErrors.prevention: Separate the scope and the price, and refer the repair.

commonErrors.error: Using a cover-up lacquer to make a fast job look finished.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the fast job as commercial preparation and state its limits.

commonErrors.error: Promising a show finish within a short time.
commonErrors.prevention: Quote the scope that the time allows.

commonErrors.error: Taking on a repair without the skill or authority.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the repair and record the referral.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not grant any licence, trade qualification or authority for repair work, electrical work, airbag work or spray painting. Completing this lesson does not qualify anyone for that work.
Describe services accurately. Claims about what a service includes must be accurate and must not leave out material facts (ACCC: false or misleading claims).

qualityStandard: Each booking is classified, and its scope and exclusions are written in the work order.
Any repair item is separated, quoted separately or referred, and the referral is recorded.
No service is described with a finish or a time it cannot deliver.
documentationEvidence: Work order with the scope tier, exclusions and any referral.
Record of each referral and the owner's acknowledgement.
summary: Detailing cleans, corrects within limits and protects; restoration reworks parts.
Classify each booking, and write its scope and exclusions down.
Refer repairs, and never describe a fast or partial job as a show finish.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the main difference between detailing and restoration?
options: Detailing costs less than restoration, so it is the cheaper option for most owners who ask
Restoration uses water and detailing does not, so the two services differ in the water used
Restoration reworks or replaces parts after dismantling; detailing cleans and treats the car as it is
There is no difference, since both services clean and treat the car in the same way for the owner

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks for a dent to be removed as part of a full detail. What is correct?
options: Treat it as a separate repair scope, quote it or refer it, and record the decision
Include it at no charge, since a small dent is part of the normal detail
Use a cover-up lacquer on the dent so that it is not visible at handover to the owner
Ignore the request and carry on with the detail as originally booked today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which description of commercial preparation is correct?
options: A show-level finish in two hours, with the full paint correction included
Restoration of a classic car, with parts rebuilt in the workshop
A minor detail to make a car presentable for sale, with its limits stated
A lifetime coating that is guaranteed to last as long as the car
